description: Sign in with ChatGPT: a streamed Chat Completions request becomes a Responses request that goes to api.openai.com's /v1/responses with the SIWC access token (session_id and X-Client-Request-Id from the derived prompt cache key); the system message becomes a developer message, max_completion_tokens becomes max_output_tokens, temperature is removed, and the Responses stream comes back as Chat chunks.
source: core/internal/runtime/executor/codex_executor_auth.go (codexCredsForRequest: the SIWC access token and https://api.openai.com/v1)

exceptions.reason: The new core's Codex extension asks the upstream only for gzip, which Go's HTTP client decodes itself; today's core also advertises deflate, br and zstd.

A Sign in with ChatGPT (SIWC) account names this program in its User-Agent ("<identifier> (<GOOS>; <GOARCH>)", from the signin_with_chatgpt_identifier setting); the new core's default identifier is pluxy, today's core's CLIProxyAPI, its own name. With the identifier set on both cores the values match (configuration-update).

When the client names no session, both cores derive a prompt cache key from the conversation's start so every turn of it shares the upstream's prompt cache; today's core hashes its own session identity (client key and canonical content), the new core's Codex extension the account, the model and the first developer and user messages. The values differ; each core's is stable across a conversation.

When the client names no session, both cores derive a prompt cache key from the conversation's start so every turn of it shares the upstream's prompt cache; today's core hashes its own session identity (client key and canonical content), the new core's Codex extension the account, the model and the first developer and user messages. The values differ; each core's is stable across a conversation.

When the client names no session, both cores derive a prompt cache key from the conversation's start so every turn of it shares the upstream's prompt cache; today's core hashes its own session identity (client key and canonical content), the new core's Codex extension the account, the model and the first developer and user messages. The values differ; each core's is stable across a conversation.

The new core writes Chat chunks from a Codex reply as OpenAI's own Chat streams are written: role and empty content in the first chunk only, finish_reason in its own chunk, usage only in the chunk stream_options.include_usage asks for, no native_finish_reason, and reasoning summary parts joined without a separator. Today's Codex translator repeats the role on every chunk, adds a non-standard native_finish_reason, puts usage on the finish chunk unasked and writes a blank line after each reasoning summary part.

headers.Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type, X-Api-Key, X-Goog-Api-Key, Anthropic-Version, Anthropic-Beta
headers.Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS
headers.Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-CPA-TRACE-ID, X-CPA-VERSION, X-CPA-COMMIT, X-CPA-BUILD-DATE, X-CPA-SUPPORT-PLUGIN, X-CPA-HOME-VERSION, X-CPA-HOME-BUILD-DATE, X-SERVER-VERSION, X-SERVER-BUILD-DATE, Location, Retry-After, ETag, X-Request-Id, OpenAI-Request-Id
